question: What is the most beneficial form of charity: money, food, or helping someone?
answer:
Our brother also asks, what form of charity is the most beneficial? And then he gives examples: giving money, or giving food, or helping others out. And the response is that the most beneficial form of charity is that which is going to help the person the most. Overall, **the most beneficial charity is that which will benefit the person in front of you the most.**

So for some people, giving food is the best charity. For others, giving money is the best charity. For others, giving of your time, of your effort: somebody needs a ride, somebody needs your car, and you say, khalas, I'll take you, no problem. For some people, smiling. Our Prophet ﷺ said smiling is charity. Time is charity. As he said in one hadith, pouring your bucket of water into your neighbor's bucket is an act of charity. So there is no one charity that everything is underneath. No, the charity that is the most beloved to Allah is the charity that is the most beneficial, and this varies from circumstance to circumstance.

And the Sunnah of our Prophet ﷺ and the actions of the righteous before us were to diversify one's charity. And this is something that unfortunately not many of us think about. When we think of charity, we think of writing a check, and that is it. And in reality, that is but one form of charity. There is charity that is beyond this: charity of your effort, physically doing something for somebody else, literally standing up and going somewhere and helping somebody out. There's charity of your physical strength. There's charity of your status, can you believe?

So if you are a person of fame, of respect, and you have connections, and somebody needs halal help (no problem, you're not doing a bribe or something, halal help), our Prophet ﷺ encouraged this. The Qur'an encourages it: whoever does a good shafa'ah. And a good shafa'ah means you use your connection for something that is legit. We're not talking about using them for the illegitimate. Somebody needs a job, and you know this brother is qualified, and you know the CEO of the company, and you call him and say, I know this brother, he is a trustworthy brother, and I encourage you to look at his resume. This is a shafa'ah. This can be charity. And subhanAllah, if you help this brother get on his feet and get a halal job, and he helps his parents and he gets married, this is the best. This brother doesn't want your check; he wants that connection that you might have that he does not have.

So my point being that there are different types of charity, and so you need to look at what is going to be the maximum benefit, and then do that. And also realize as well that yes, it is true that there are certain ahadith about certain types of charities, and so try to diversify. Don't just do one thing. For example, our Prophet ﷺ in particular encouraged the helping of the orphans. And in particular, when a man came to him and said, "O Messenger of Allah, my heart becomes hard," our Prophet ﷺ said, "Go and feed a hungry person, and wipe the hair," or the head, "of the orphan." It means hug the orphan.

Love is charity, dear brothers and sisters. So loving an orphan: the orphan does not have a father figure, and you become a part of that person's life and you are there. So look at what he said: give food to the hungry and wipe the head of that child, imsah ra's al-yatim. Why? Because what that yatim is missing the most is the love of a father. And so if you step in and you take on a fatherly figure, that is charity. You're spending your time and your love, and you're showing your dedication.

So diversify. Just like the income analysts, the wealth generators, tell us to diversify our investments: invest in this stock, and invest in mutual funds, and invest in real estate, and invest in this and that. They say don't put all your eggs in one basket. So we as well, when we invest for the sake of Allah, don't want to invest in only one. We diversify, because we do not know which du'a of which brother will be the most beneficial for us. We want to do as much as possible.

And, for example, one of the best charities is to build water wells. This is something that was very common in the Muslim ummah. Throughout our history, one of the most significant charities that was always done is to have a public water source, because everybody will benefit and they will thank you for it. In those days they didn't have running water. So people would dig a well, and then they would just leave it there and say, waqf fi sabilillah: anybody can drink from it. So much so that our Prophet even said that if a bird or an animal drinks from that water, you will get the reward for it.

So these are things that we should think about: diversifying our charity, making the maximum amount of benefit, and also for the longest time. So you're asking which charity is the best? I said that which is of maximum benefit, and also that which goes beyond one instance in time. So the longest impact to the greatest number of people: that's what you should be thinking about. And so having a charity that is perpetual (it's called a waqf) is better than a one-off charity. And a simple example, as I explained, is building a well, or constructing something that people can benefit from for longer generations, for multiple times. And that's going to be considered a charity.
